discovery: Squeezed states of light to surpass the quantum noise limit in precision interferometry and gravitational-wave detection
motivation: Caves showed in 1981 that the quantum noise limiting interferometers comes from vacuum fluctuations entering the unused port, and that injecting squeezed vacuum could beat the shot-noise limit. It took decades of careful experimental work to turn this into a real tool. Schnabel's group built squeezed-light sources with record noise suppression across the detection band and put squeezing into continuous operation at GEO600. Mavalvala led the development and integration of squeezed-vacuum injection in Advanced LIGO. Since the O3 run, all major detectors have used squeezing, and frequency-dependent squeezing now reduces quantum noise across the full band, which increases the rate of detected astrophysical events. This is the clearest case of nonclassical light going from a textbook curiosity to an essential part of a frontier observatory. Each noise reduction was verified by rigorous, calibrated measurement, and it changed how physicists think about quantum limits to measurement.
